draft.title: Gallipoli
card: On 25 April 1915 Australian and New Zealand troops landed at Gallipoli, a peninsula in Turkey. The Ottoman Empire, Turkey's ruler, was fighting on Germany's side.
The Allies hoped to open a sea route to Russia and knock the Ottoman Empire out of the war. The troops landed on a steep, narrow beach, later called Anzac Cove.
Ottoman defenders held the high ground above the beach. The Allies could not break out, and the fighting became a stalemate.
After about eight months and heavy losses on both sides, the Allies withdrew in December 1915. The campaign failed to reach its aims.
draft.remember: Gallipoli was a failed Allied campaign that began on 25 April 1915 and ended in withdrawal.

a.q: What was the outcome of the Gallipoli campaign for the Allies?
opts: They withdrew after months of fighting, their aims unmet
They captured the peninsula and reached Russia by sea
They won a quick victory in the first week of fighting
They signed a peace treaty with the Ottoman Empire
a.why: The Ottoman defenders held the high ground, the fighting stalled, and the Allies left in December 1915. The campaign did not succeed.
a.clue: Think about who held the high ground.

b.q: Mia reads a letter from a soldier who landed at Anzac Cove in April 1915. In which country was he fighting?
opts: Turkey
France
Belgium
Egypt
b.why: Gallipoli is a peninsula in Turkey, then part of the Ottoman Empire. France and Belgium were the sites of the Western Front, a different theatre.

problems.detail: 'The Allies withdrew in December 1915' is imprecise. Anzac and Suvla were evacuated in December 1915, but the British and French at Cape Helles did not leave until 9 January 1916. Better: 'the Anzacs withdrew in December 1915' or 'the last Allied troops left in January 1916'. Why (a) repeats the claim.
